title: Strix Writer — Open-source editor for STEM assessments, unit-aware math, and engineering reports
description: Write, calculate, and grade in a single living document: structured word processing, parametric math with dimensional analysis, 2D CAD, plane structures, and step-by-step worked solutions. Open source for Windows, macOS, Linux, FreeBSD, and Web.
socialAlt: Strix Writer: write, calculate, and grade on a single sheet
heroKicker: For educators and engineers · Open Source · Alpha
heroLead: Strix Writer combines structured document layout and parametric computation in one living document: change an input value or switch between variants A, B, and C to instantly recompute unit-checked equations, 2D CAD drawings, structural diagrams, answer keys, and grades.
shotCalcAlt: Strix Writer showing a physics calculation: a car accelerating from rest, acceleration derived from speeds in km/h and time, force, distance with step-by-step worked algebra, and a verified dimensional check
stat1Text: of question in a single exam: calculation, multiple choice, true/false, open answer, CAD drawing, cloze, matching, worked example
stat2Text: parametric data variants, each recalculating worked solutions and figures automatically
stat3Text: criterion-based scores table that totals points and maps grades as you type
stat4Text: one independent file per exercise, assembled via Master Document without altering source files
pillarsTitle: Three tools in one living document
p1Text: Styles, tables, graph paper, accessibility presets (dyslexia-friendly), and scoring rubrics ready for print or export to PDF and LaTeX.
p2Text: Equations in natural mathematical notation with dimensional analysis and unit checking that automatically drive technical drawings, scientific plots, and structural analyses.
p3Text: From symbolic formula isolation to numerical substitution and the final result—generated on demand to produce both the student handout and the teacher’s answer key in one click.
howTitle: From the first exercise to final grades
a1Text: Every exercise runs in an isolated calculation sandbox for given data, formulas, and unit-checked results. Switch between variants A, B, and C for adjacent rows of desks, and worked solutions, parametric figures, and summaries update automatically.
a2Text: Combine calculation problems, multiple choice, true/false, open answers with configurable space in cm or graph paper, parametric 2D CAD drawings, cloze completion, matching, and worked examples while keeping pagination identical when solutions are hidden.
a3Text: Keep one file per exercise indexed by grade, subject, duration, and points. A Master Document assembles assessments and exams with cover pages, numbering, and dyslexia-friendly accessibility presets without modifying source files.
a4Text: Question points feed a criterion-based scores table (awarded vs. available points) totalled live across rows and columns, while built-in or custom grading scales convert totals directly into final marks.
exTitle: One file for the student handout, the worked answer key, and the grading rubric
exIntro: The Teaching tab brings together every stage of exam preparation. Exercises sit inside protected structural controls: edit prose and equations freely while keeping prompts, answer spaces, and summaries intact.
ex1: Multi-step calculation problems: statement, parametric data equations, three-level nested sub-questions, step-by-step worked solutions under each prompt, and a unified results summary.
ex2: Pagination-invariant answer toggling: ticked choices, hidden cloze words, and CAD answer layers disappear on the student handout while answer spaces retain their exact height.
ex3: Master Document assembly: pull exercises from your archive filtered by topic or duration; cover pages, numbering, and display toggles belong to the master.
ex4: Criterion scores table & grading scale: one row per exercise, paired columns per rubric criterion, and automatic grade mapping with presets for Italy, Switzerland, Germany, France, or custom curves.
ex5: Accessibility presets & one-step pack export: combinable dyslexia-friendly presets (reading, writing, numeracy, and memory), pre-flight validation, and batch export of student PDFs plus the teacher’s synoptic key.
shotExerciseAlt: A Strix Writer exercise with parametric data in two variants, lettered sub-questions, and live step-by-step worked solutions beneath each prompt
mathTitle: Natural mathematical notation that executes as live code
mathIntro: Equations written on the page evaluate top-to-bottom in reading order. Dimensional or syntax errors are isolated inline with ⚠ diagnostics without halting downstream calculations.
math1: A single = statement: defines parameters, evaluates expressions, isolates unknowns symbolically (degree 1–2 polynomials, powers, roots, exponentials, trigonometry), or solves nonlinear equations numerically.
math2: Dimensional analysis & unit checking: upright colour-coded SI and engineering units with automatic conversion and case-mismatch hints (such as kN).
math3: Step-by-step worked solutions: symbolic algebraic isolation, numerical substitution with units, and rounded final values aligned cleanly at =.
math4: Calculus, summations & vectors: derivatives, definite integrals, ∑, ∏, ranges 1..5, and typed unit vectors with decimal or significant-figure formatting.
math5: Inline design checks: parametric comparisons such as σ ≤ f_yd verify engineering limits directly inside your report.
mathFigureLabel: Symbolic solving, dimensional unit checking, and a calculated lab table inside a Strix Writer document
tableCaption: A calculated laboratory table: unit-typed column headers, an automatic density formula, statistical mean, and automatic exposure of each column as a vector.
cadTitle: Technical 2D geometry driven directly by worksheet variables
cadIntro: CAD drawings sit inline on the page while binding coordinates, lengths, and dimensions to parameters defined above: update b = 8cm and both the geometry and its dimensions redraw immediately.
cad1: Parameter-driven labels: {{L}} renders the computed quantity, {{L:both}} renders symbol and value, and <> reads true measured geometry.
cad2: Full-featured 2D CAD sheet: lines, arcs, circles, polylines, baseline/continue dimensions, and hatches; move, rotate, mirror, offset, trim, extend, fillet, and typed coordinate entry.
cad3: Exact geometry kernel: true-curve object snaps (endpoint, midpoint, centre, intersection, perpendicular, tangent) verified to 10⁻⁹ precision.
cad4: Expression-preserving grips: dragging a parametric vertex updates its symbolic expression to L + 0.5 m instead of overwriting it with a raw number.
cad5: Layers, lineweights & completion figures: dedicated answer layers stay visible in the teacher key and hide automatically on the student’s squared drawing grid.
cadFigureLabel: A parametric right triangle with associative dimensions showing b = 8 cm and h = 6 cm
cadCaption: The triangle’s vertices are bound to ["b", 0] and [0, "h"]: changing b or h updates the drawing and its dimensions together.
structTitle: Beams, frames, and trusses solved inline with full algebraic working
structIntro: Insert continuous beams, portal frames, or trusses directly into reports or exams: Strix Writer classifies determinacy and draws loads, support reactions, and hatched axial (N), shear (T), and bending moment (M) diagrams to scale.
struct1: Arbitrary plane systems: fixed ends, pins, rollers, inclined links and sliders, internal hinges, point loads, couples, and trapezoidal distributed loads across statically determinate or indeterminate structures.
struct2: Parametric & textbook-ready: spans and loads reference worksheet variables so every exam variant gets recalculated diagrams, with configurable tension-side conventions, sign badges, and stations.
struct3: Full-page Structure Editor: grid snapping, a 360° graduated vector protractor, interactive grips, and parametric tables for nodes, members, supports, and loads.
struct4: Step-by-step worked equilibrium: free-body diagrams, load resultants and moment arms, algebraic equilibrium equations, virtual-work force method integrals, and section-cut laws N(x), T(x), M(x).
struct5: One-click Report ↔ Exercise switch: turn any solved structure into a six-part student exercise with blank diagram panels on the student copy, or switch back to a technical report.
shotStructureAlt: Simply supported beam in Strix Writer driven by parameters L, q, and F, showing loads, support reactions, shear and bending moment diagrams, and the Structure Editor
plotTitle: Experimental data, curve fitting, and function analysis without external spreadsheets
plotIntro: Tabulate laboratory measurements in calculated tables and plot mathematical curves linked live to document parameters and exam variants.
plot1: Unit-aware calculated tables: column headers assign symbol, unit, and formula across rows; every column immediately becomes a typed vector usable in equations and plots.
plot2: Cartesian, parametric & polar curves: scientific axes with automatic unit conversion, custom line styles, and formula legends.
plot3: Lab uncertainty & regression: experimental data series with error bars, curve fitting, and built-in statistical functions (mean, median, variance, standard deviation, slope, and R²).
plot4: Live analytical readouts: roots, extrema, tangent lines, and definite integrals are computed over the domain and written beneath the plot as live equations.
shotPlotAlt: Scientific function plot in Strix Writer displaying roots, extrema, a tangent line, shaded definite integral area, and the Plot Properties pane
agTitle: Command-driven architecture for batch scripts and autonomous agents
agIntro: Every operation in Strix Writer is a deterministic command with a stable ID and typed parameters. The ribbon UI, CLI, local control channel, and MCP server dispatch the exact same commands—never opening blocking modal dialogs during programmatic runs.
agMcpComment2: or drive a live desktop window
agNote: Both the control channel and MCP server bind strictly to 127.0.0.1, require a per-window authentication key, and support explicit read/write directory confinement.
featTitle: Everything needed from engineering calculation sheets to printed exam packs
featIntro: Capabilities shipping in Strix Writer today, alongside upcoming items on the public roadmap.
f1Text: Each exercise acts as an independent calculation sandbox: multiple problems in the same exam can define <var>t</var> or <var>L</var> without collision while recalculating their own variants.
f2Text: Calculation with handwritten answer lines and tolerances, multiple choice with per-variant shuffling, aligned true/false batteries, open space, CAD drawing, cloze, matching, and worked examples.
f3Text: One file per exercise tagged with educational metadata; Master Documents assemble complete exams while leaving source archive files untouched.
f4Text: Paired awarded/available columns per rubric criterion, live totals, and preset or custom grading scales for Italy, Switzerland, Germany, France, and percentage systems.
f5Text: Full SI prefix support, dimensional homogeneity checks, symbolic degree 1–2 solvers with physical domain filters, and on-demand step-by-step algebra.
f6Text: Four combinable accessibility presets (reading, writing, numeracy, memory) on clean white pages, plus crisp vector graph paper at any zoom and in PDF.
f7Text: Worksheet-driven coordinates, exact curve snaps, associative dimensions, hatches, and toggleable answer layers for student completion tasks.
f8Text: Paragraph and character styles, multi-column sections, tables, headers/footers, comments, tracked changes, multilingual spellchecking, and clean PDF, LaTeX, HTML, and Markdown export.
f10Text: Unit-scaled axes, error bars, linear and nonlinear regression, plus live equations for zeros, extrema, tangents, and definite integrals.
f11Title: Static solver & N, T, M diagrams
f11Text: Stiffness and force-method analysis of beams, frames, and trusses with textbook internal-force diagrams and live step-by-step equilibrium working.
f12Text: Automated validation of variants, missing keys, and point totals before exporting student PDFs, accessibility editions, and the teacher’s synoptic answer key together.
f9Title: Native on desktop and instant via WebAssembly
f9Text: A single pure-Rust codebase running natively on Windows, macOS, Linux, and FreeBSD and in any modern browser, localized in English, Italian, German, and French with light and dark themes.
plannedText: Expected-value verification tables and per-variant synoptic previews in pre-flight checks; ordering questions; multi-region equation systems and matrices; dimensional geometric constraints in the CAD editor.
trustTitle: Local-first by design, stored in inspectable open formats
t1Text: No mandatory sign-ups, no usage analytics, and no automatic crash uploads. Your documents, exercise bank, and preferences stay strictly on your machine.
t2Text: Production crates forbid unwrap, expect, and unsafe; every command is tested against hostile inputs and backed by automatic recovery snapshots.
t3Text: Native .xmath files are standard OOXML archives, complemented by round-trip DOCX preservation of live calculation objects, ODT and RTF import, and export to PDF, LaTeX, HTML, and Markdown.
t4Text: Dual-licensed under MIT or Apache-2.0, developed in the open, with full attribution documented for every bundled font, dictionary, and translation.
dlIntro: Native installers, portable builds, and a zero-install WebAssembly edition. Strix Writer is currently in alpha: keep backups of critical documents and report issues on GitHub.
dlWindowsNote: Windows 10 and 11. Builds are not yet code-signed, so SmartScreen may prompt on first launch. The portable executable requires no installation and stores settings in a local StrixData folder.
dlMacNote: Single universal binary running natively on both Apple silicon and Intel Macs.
dlLinuxNote: Native packages for x86_64 and aarch64; riscv64 builds provided as deb, rpm, and tar.gz.
dlBsdNote: Desktop application and CLI binary packaged with icons and licence files.
dlWebNote: The full application compiled to WebAssembly—ideal for locked-down school lab computers with nothing to install. Download the static ZIP to self-host on an intranet.
